analysis: Welfare and public policy best fits the four-discipline common core and the illustrated thematic package. Ethics, political philosophy, agency and judgment frame normative questions; public economics examines taxation and social insurance; modern, gender and imperial history ground institutions in context; policy analysis and three forms of research methods support inquiry. Philosophy of mind, advanced calculus and behavioral economics were replaced in that plan with historical breadth, a historical research course and direct policy analysis. The market-regulation plan keeps economics and quantitative methods, including econometrics and behavioral economics, and adds constitutional and international law, EU law and EU politics. Together they distinguish it from the closest plan. The sustainability plan includes biodiversity and farming impacts, water management, climate science, energy transition and geospatial evidence, with policy analysis, public economics, ethics and climate justice. This supplies the substance for the official sustainability interests beyond generic environmental content. Democracy remains substantively represented in the closest plan through comparative institutions and democratic backsliding, political philosophy, modern history and policy. The fourth thematic package was considered and its interests are covered within the closest plan, with the available three slots occupied by distinct designs. The advanced external options lack full published topic details, and the integrated package and required two-discipline thesis have no directly equivalent UCR component.
